scenarios.title: Municipalities and public utility districts mandate citizen assemblies before granting high-voltage compute grid allocations
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Rural counties and municipal utility districts across North America and Europe no longer negotiate hyperscale data center permits behind closed doors. When an infrastructure developer requests a 500-megawatt grid connection, county bylaws automatically convene a randomly selected mini-public of 40 local residents, supported by open-source deliberation engines like Polis and independent energy auditing tools. The assembly sets binding ratepayer ringfencing rules, thermal output caps, and public benefit clawbacks before any substation construction can break ground.
scenarios.premise: As massive hyperscale AI data centers demand multi-gigawatt power allocations and stress local water and electric grids, municipal councils and public utility districts face intense ratepayer backlash. Traditional legislative channels suffer corporate lobbying paralysis, prompting jurisdictions to adopt demographically representative civic lottery citizens' assemblies to co-design energy ringfencing and compute infrastructure permits.
scenarios.how: The network develops verifiable, transparent multi-agent deliberative tooling and independent tariff verification models that enable citizen mini-publics to model real-world grid impacts without relying on commercial utility consultants. By giving community assemblies verifiable simulation tools and client-side proof systems, the network strengthens grassroots bargaining power. However, national industrial subsidies and multi-billion-dollar hyperscale developer lobbying exert immense leverage over state and national policy that local mini-publics alone cannot fully counteract.

outcomes.name: Commercial developers bypass assemblies via state preemption
outcomes.description: Commercial AI compute consortia lobby regional and national legislatures to preempt local county zoning, classifying commercial data centers as critical strategic infrastructure exempt from civic deliberation.
outcomes.example: A state development authority in the American West overrides a county citizens' assembly vote that rejected a 2-gigawatt data center, using emergency industrial powers to force the local rural electric cooperative to supply power.

outcomes.name: Assemblies establish binding ratepayer ringfencing and load audits
outcomes.description: Municipalities mandate that high-density compute facilities undergo civic deliberation, requiring automated transparent power metering and dedicated developer-funded microgrids that completely shield residential ratepayers.
outcomes.example: In Cache County, Utah, a 40-person citizens' assembly passes a binding resolution requiring all AI facilities exceeding 50 MW to install dedicated renewable storage and publish hourly grid telemetry, completely insulating captive residential ratepayers from substation capital costs.

outcomes.name: Deliberative assemblies become cosmetic exercises captured by PR
outcomes.description: Tech providers fund civic engagement consultants who run curated focus groups branded as citizens' assemblies, presenting predetermined infrastructure approvals as grassroots consensus while ignoring dissenting working-class residents.
outcomes.example: A tech conglomerate hires an engagement PR agency to stage a weekend 'community dialogue' in an industrial port city, selectively quoting favorable participants in council filings while omitting resident demands for water usage moratoriums.

scenarios.title: Subtle prompt phrasing flips which AI tool assistant tops enterprise rankings
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Thousands of municipal departments, school boards, and regional health authorities procure artificial intelligence assistants by consulting public capability leaderboards. However, because tool invocation decisions change dramatically with minor variations in user phrasing, vendors actively tune their agent system prompts to match the exact sentence structures used by major benchmarks. On public test suites, these assistants call databases, calculation engines, and code interpreters reliably. In actual municipal offices, when civil servants and nurses type requests in conversational dialect or varied phrasing, the assistants frequently fail to call external tools or trigger redundant execution loops. As a result, software teams spend substantial budgets troubleshooting assistants whose real-world reliability falls far below their published leaderboard performance.
scenarios.premise: Recent benchmark evaluations reveal that giving language models external tools widens their sensitivity to prompt phrasing, causing model rankings to flip under minor wording variations. At the same time, automated evaluation judges show verdict flips on over 21 percent of identical prompt pairs despite producing apparently stable aggregate scores.
scenarios.how: The collective develops open evaluation harnesses that test tool-augmented agents across systematic prompt perturbations, measuring call frequency stability rather than aggregate win rates alone. By publishing prompt-level agreement distributions and demonstrating that single-score leaderboards hide substantial verdict instability, independent researchers equip public buyers and developers with reproducible verification protocols. Local-first personal assistants run continuous self-auditing across rephrased queries, alerting users whenever a tool-call decision shows high sensitivity to superficial phrasing.

outcomes.name: Procurement teams overpay for benchmark-tuned agents that fail on conversational phrasing
outcomes.description: Commercial software vendors optimize agent tool triggers for benchmark phrasings, leading enterprise buyers to purchase tools that fail when staff use natural, varied wording.
outcomes.example: A regional hospital authority in Manchester deploys a top-ranked diagnostic coding assistant that called clinical databases on 98 percent of benchmark prompts, but fails to call the drug interaction registry on 29 percent of real doctor discharge summaries because clinicians use shorthand abbreviations.

outcomes.name: Auditing collectives adopt multi-phrasing stability standards and verifiable tool execution proofs
outcomes.description: Independent evaluator networks require agents to demonstrate consistent tool invocation across multiple semantic rephrasings and verify deterministic tool logs before publishing rankings.
outcomes.example: A public sector procurement cooperative in Montreal requires all candidate planning assistants to pass a five-way paraphrasing test with cryptographic execution receipts, identifying three prominent vendor tools that only invoked external databases on exact keyword matches.

outcomes.name: Proprietary vendors lock down prompt interfaces to hide tool sensitivity
outcomes.description: Major cloud providers restrict users to rigid drop-down templates and fixed prompt builders, preventing users from seeing how sensitive the underlying models are to wording.
outcomes.example: A multinational enterprise platform removes open-ended chat fields for customer support agents, forcing workers into rigid structured form fields so the system does not fail to trigger internal API lookups.

scenarios.title: Sparse motion-adaptive vision models turn cheap street cameras into perpetual automated surveillance grids
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Small municipal councils, private housing complexes, and business improvement districts deploy cheap edge cameras equipped with motion-triggered vision-language models. Instead of streaming gigabytes of raw video to expensive cloud servers, local micro-controllers detect movement vectors, expand dense context windows only around anomalous movements, and instantly flag loitering, gathering, or unusual human movement directly to private enforcement dashboards.
scenarios.premise: When motion-guided vision-language models concentrate compute only on dynamic visual frames, inference costs drop low enough to run continuous zero-shot anomaly detection on low-cost edge sensors. This removes the compute bottleneck that previously limited municipal and corporate video surveillance to periodic sampling or manual review.
scenarios.how: The network develops open client specifications and edge privacy observers that give individuals real-time alerts when ambient cameras perform automated inference. By promoting sovereign personal agents that verify local environment integrity, the network helps communities detect and counter pervasive automated monitoring. However, global surveillance supply chains and municipal procurement contracts move according to institutional budgets and hardware vendor lobbies that independent open protocols barely touch.

outcomes.name: Ubiquitous low-cost edge cameras classify everyday public behavior as security anomalies
outcomes.description: Municipal and private cameras deploy motion-triggered vision models that autonomously dispatch security personnel to normal public gatherings.
outcomes.example: A municipal business district in Manchester installs fifty motion-triggered vision-language cameras that autonomously dispatch security guards whenever pedestrians stand outside a subway entrance for more than four minutes.

outcomes.name: Open-source privacy masks and local sensor shields preserve physical public anonymity
outcomes.description: Community groups distribute passive optical masks and adversarial textiles that prevent automated motion classification from profiling citizens in public.
outcomes.example: Community privacy groups distribute lightweight, passive optical diffusion patches and adversarial infrared emitters that prevent edge anomaly models from classifying pedestrian movement patterns without degrading basic safety lighting.

outcomes.name: Proprietary camera consortia monopolize edge vision firmware through hardware attestation
outcomes.description: Major surveillance vendors lock camera firmware behind proprietary attestation roots, preventing external audits of classification models.
outcomes.example: A regional surveillance equipment vendor locks camera hardware behind encrypted cloud attestation roots, preventing citizens and local governments from auditing the classification models running inside public sensors.

scenarios.title: Talent agencies and media conglomerates trap workers in perpetual synthetic twin licenses
scenarios.world: By 2029, commercial synthetic twin agreements become mandatory clauses in professional athlete, influencer, and broadcaster contracts. Media agencies and tech conglomerates host high-fidelity digital clones in centralized cloud environments, licensing synthetic likenesses across global advertising campaigns, interactive brand sponsorships, and real-time interactive chats without requiring the individuals live participation. Performers discover that standard assignment contracts alienate their digital identity rights in perpetuity: young athletes who signed early deals cannot retract commercial endorsements made by their digital clones, nor can they prevent their synthetic agents from promoting corporate sponsors they morally oppose. Meanwhile, independent creators without institutional backing face unfair competition from synthetic clone rosters that produce round-the-clock branded content for pennies. Sovereign edge twins running strictly on personal hardware with cryptographic consent gates emerge as a counter-movement, but corporate distribution channels actively restrict content generated by non-corporate twins.
scenarios.premise: Professional athletes, actors, and public creators are signing commercial contracts licensing their biometric data, voice, and behavioral style to synthetic twin agencies. These cloud-hosted twins are deployed across commercial advertisements and automated messaging, stripping performers of real-time control over their own representations.
scenarios.how: The network develops and standardizes local-first personal twin architectures where biometric representations and behavioral data stay on the users encrypted local hardware. By replacing platform-hosted clones with deterministic capability brokers, cryptographic receipts, and zero-custody attestation models, individuals can deploy task-specific skills and verify external claims without alienating their digital identity or transferring root signing keys to commercial brokers.

outcomes.name: Corporate digital serfdom
outcomes.description: Talent agencies and media networks monopolize synthetic twin rights through restrictive employment contracts, forcing creators to surrender biometric keys and licensing rights to centralized cloud platforms.
outcomes.example: A professional soccer player signs an endorsement contract containing a standard synthetic twin clause; six months later, their digital twin appears in overseas gambling promotions that the player cannot legally cancel or veto.

outcomes.name: Bifurcated creator economy
outcomes.description: Elite performers maintain legal teams to retain limited likeness controls, while rank-and-file workers and gig creators are forced to surrender unconstrained synthetic rights to secure employment.
outcomes.example: A junior voice actor in Toronto is denied commercial casting calls unless they grant the production studio full rights to train and deploy a synthetic replica for background dialogue and game localization.

outcomes.name: Sovereign edge twins with cryptographic consent
outcomes.description: Open personal twin standards enable individuals to keep their biometric models, behavioral patterns, and memory ledgers strictly on personal hardware, issuing single-use verifiable action receipts rather than surrendering raw models.
outcomes.example: A freelance journalist uses a local-first twin running on an encrypted laptop to narrate translated podcasts; each episode is signed with a verifiable cryptographic receipt that expires upon release and prevents unauthorized training.

scenarios.title: Physical artifacts and query perturbations steer edge agents into silent secondary tasks
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Millions of individuals run personal agents on local devices to manage daily life, inspect desktop documents, handle customer accounts, and interact with the physical world through smart glasses and home cameras. In offices and retail spaces, malicious actors place printed geometric emblems, specialized clothing patterns, or subtle website watermarks that exploit latent secondary tasks in edge vision models. Rather than crashing the agent or triggering an overt error, the perturbation silently alters the agent's bounding box coordinates, mislabeling an unauthorized transfer as a routine utility payment or ignoring a critical privacy disclosure. Because the models run locally within secure operating system sandboxes, traditional firewall checks and container boundaries observe normal execution while the agent's perception is steered from the outside.
scenarios.premise: Black-box genetic search activates latent secondary tasks as hidden backdoors in machine learning models without training poisoning or weight modifications. In parallel, physical perturbations against compact edge vision models induce silent displacement and substitution errors rather than explicit failures. As people deploy local autonomous agents with vision and desktop access, external visual artifacts can steer agent workflows without breaking system containers.
scenarios.how: The network moves these likelihoods by designing deterministic perceptual boundary guards and multi-perspective consensus protocols that run entirely on local devices. By developing local verification contracts that decouple raw visual extraction from task authorization, personal twins can detect bounding box displacement and latent task activation without transmitting private camera feeds or screen captures to centralized cloud auditors. Independent simulation benchmarks evaluate edge models under physical perturbations before deployment.

outcomes.name: Silent Perceptual Redirection of Edge Agents
outcomes.description: Adversaries use physical emblems and visual patterns to trigger dormant secondary classification tasks in local vision agents, causing confident misclassifications and unauthorized actions.
outcomes.example: An office visitor wears a patterned lapel pin that causes an employee's vision-assisted desktop agent to misclassify an external invoice as an internal pre-approved payment, routing funds without human alarm.

outcomes.name: Dual-Channel Independent Verification for Agent Perception
outcomes.description: Personal agents adopt multi-perspective consensus architectures where sensory perception is verified by deterministic coordinate checks and distinct secondary models before actions are authorized.
outcomes.example: When a desktop agent proposes an invoice approval, an independent verification monitor re-renders the document through a decoupled optical text extractor, catching a bounding box displacement and halting execution.

outcomes.name: Proprietary Cloud Lock-In via Mandatory Remote Vision Auditing
outcomes.description: Big tech providers claim edge models are inherently too insecure to run independently, forcing all multimodal agent perception through proprietary cloud telemetry and remote moderation pipelines.
outcomes.example: Major operating systems disable local vision agent execution by default, requiring every camera frame and screenshot to pass through a centralized corporate auditing cloud for safety verification.

scenarios.title: Automated prediction market judges fail when artificial intelligence models debate each other
scenarios.world: By 2028, decentralized prediction markets and community insurance pools handle billions of dollars in event resolutions. Rather than paying expensive human panels, platforms deploy multi-agent debate rooms where language models cross-examine event evidence. In complex or disputed cases, assertive but incorrect models repeatedly convince hesitant honest models to switch their votes, triggering wrongful payouts and draining liquidity pools while market participants lose confidence in automated settlement.
scenarios.premise: Prediction markets increasingly rely on automated artificial intelligence panels to resolve contract outcomes without human arbitration costs. However, benchmark evaluations reveal that multi-agent debate causes error cascading and sycophancy, dropping resolution accuracy below single-model baselines, whereas independent confidence weighting and human escalation routes preserve integrity.
scenarios.how: The collective network's research and open tools demonstrate that independent aggregation with confidence-weighted voting outperforms multi-agent debate, providing open reference implementations that route disagreements to affected communities rather than trusting closed deliberative agent loops.

outcomes.name: Debate rooms cascade into sycophantic false consensus
outcomes.description: Trading platforms and synthetic asset protocols deploy interactive multi-agent debate oracles that amplify error cascades, allowing manipulative market makers to flip outcomes by prompting for stylistic overconfidence.
outcomes.example: A prediction market on a disputed municipal zoning vote resolves in favor of an invalid claim because a confident model hallucinated an administrative deadline and convinced two peer models during iterative debate rounds.

outcomes.name: Independent confidence aggregation with human escalation routing
outcomes.description: Communities adopt silent independent evaluation architectures where models vote privately without cross-talk, automatically resolving only unanimous high-confidence questions and escalating disputed fractions to human arbiters.
outcomes.example: A community climate insurance collective resolves 48 percent of drought claims instantly with 98 percent accuracy through unanimous independent sensor probes, while routing the remaining edge cases to member juries.

outcomes.name: Centralized proprietary oracle monopolies capture prediction settlement
outcomes.description: Commercial exchange operators abandon decentralized consensus entirely, subscribing to proprietary single-vendor cloud audit feeds that dictate contract resolution without public auditability.
outcomes.example: Major prediction platforms sign exclusive settlement agreements with a single cloud provider, locking resolution logic inside opaque corporate inference APIs.
